hints: Unfold each bounce into a straight diagonal path through mirrored copies of the grid.
The ball returns to the starting corner after twice the least common multiple of n-1 and m-1 steps.
A cell is visited exactly when its zero-based coordinates x,y satisfy x = y or x = -y modulo 2g, where g=gcd(n-1,m-1).
analogy: Imagine tiling the plane with mirror images of the board: the bouncing path becomes a straight line.
example: For a 3 by 4 board, the side lengths are 2 and 3. The first return takes 12 steps and the ball visits 6 distinct cells.
algorithm: Set a=n-1, b=m-1, g=gcd(a,b), A=a/g, B=b/g. Let E(q)=(q+1)//2 and O(q)=q//2 count even and odd numbers in 0..q-1. The return time is 2*lcm(a,b); the distinct count is E(A+1)*E(B+1)+O(A+1)*O(B+1)+(g-1)*A*B. Use wide integers.
correctness: Unfolding shows that folded coordinates (x,y) occur exactly when x equals y or -y modulo 2g. When both coordinates are multiples of g the two congruences overlap, contributing the parity-matching first two terms. For each of the other g-1 residues, the two congruences are disjoint and contribute A*B cells. The unfolded position first returns to both zero boundaries after 2*lcm(a,b) steps.
complexity: O(log min(n,m)) time and O(1) space per test case.
